body: claimed: research agent (Opus, coordinator) · 2026-11-20T07:52Z · no branch · plan: research

Research result (part 1 of 2): where the first move comes from. All references are on `origin/main` at `ab9955105`. I did not build or run anything. Each statement below comes from the source and from the recorded goldens.

## The operation calculation (the cause)

1. Almost all 2D and 3D milling generators seed their path builder at the zero of the frame, on the clearance plane: `PathBuilder::approached(Point3::new(0.0, 0.0, p.clearance_z))`. Examples:
   - `crates/motion/src/machining2d/face.rs:214`, `pocket.rs:305`, `contour_whole.rs:242`, `contour_chain.rs:82`, `slots.rs:161`, `bore.rs:266`, `circular.rs:268`, `chamfer.rs:131`, `rest2d.rs:255`, `adaptive/rest/post.rs:24`.
   - `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/raster.rs:190`, `flat.rs:71`, `pencil.rs:240`, `shadow.rs:245`, `polar.rs:28`, `rings.rs:522`, `morph.rs:178`, `flow.rs:87`, `geodesic.rs:300`, `deburr.rs:296`, `swarf.rs:34`.
2. The first move of the path is a rapid out of that seed, on the clearance plane, to the entry point (`crates/cl/src/cl/path_approach.rs:60-72`).
3. #2382 then moves the START of that rapid to the WCS origin of the setup: `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:3109-3117` calls `Toolpath::seat_approach` (`crates/cl/src/cl/path_approach.rs:30-49`). The doc comment says it plainly: "the drawn approach, the simulation and the checks read the WCS origin". The test `crates/app/tests/wcs_start.rs:143-170` (`opens_at`) locks this: the first move must start at the G54 origin.
4. Thus each 2D and 3D milling path has a first move from (WCS X0 Y0, clearance) to the entry. The machine never makes this move. After a tool change the X/Y position of the tool is not known.

## The post (correct in the usual case)

1. The posts write only the END of a move. `fanuc.cps:850-857` (`onRapid`) writes the target. The first X/Y traverse after each tool call goes through `xyFirst` (`fanuc.cps:833-848`): a Z-only `G00` to the clearance, then `G00 X Y` of the target. The same law (#1616, #1633) is in all milling posts (`grblhal.cps:550-566`, `haas`, `heidenhain`, `linuxcnc`, `mach4`, `mazak`, `doosan-dnm`, `tinyg`, `tormach`, `carvera`, `sinumerik`).
2. The engine calls `onToolChange` for each section, also for a repeated tool (`crates/post/src/post/tool_change.rs:5,57-67`). `fanuc.cps:666-675` then sets `xyUnknown = true` again. So each section starts with this law.
3. Golden reading, `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/face_square_40x40.nc` (CL: `START 0 0 5000`, `Rapid -5000 5000 5000`): the posted program has `G00 Z5.` then `G00 X-5. Y5. Z5.`. It does not write `X0 Y0`. The doosan-dnm and haas goldens are the same.
4. `crates/app/tests/wcs_start.rs:180-209` posts a face, a 3D finish and a drill with G54 on the stock corner. It asserts that the first X/Y block is the end of the opening rapid, not the origin.
5. The `G28 X0 Y0` (`fanuc.cps:240`) and `G0 G53 X0 Y0` (`sinumerik.cps:530`) blocks are machine-home moves at the end of the program or after an operation. They are not in the WCS and are not this defect.
6. The goldens `nc/grblhal/altmill_4x4_two_tool.nc` show `G0 X0 Y0`. This is from a hand-written stream that rapids to X0 Y0 (`crates/app/tests/altmill_machines.rs:23`). It is not this defect.

No golden has a WCS origin that is not at the world zero, so the goldens cannot show the difference between a WCS at the centre and at a corner. Only `wcs_start.rs` has that case.

## One case where the wrong start reaches the posted G-code

`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:3191-3203` sends the path to `fixture_route::plan_links` before the post. The opening rapid is a link (a run of rapids). If the line from the WCS origin to the entry, at the clearance, strikes a fixture box, `plan` (`crates/app/src/operation/fixture_route.rs:186-229`) lays new moves:
- up at the start X/Y (the WCS origin) to the height `H`,
- across to the entry X/Y at `H`,
- down to the entry.

The first new rapid ends at (WCS origin, `H`). The post writes it: `G00 Z<H>`, then `G00 X0. Y0. Z<H>` in the WCS. Thus the tool really goes to the WCS origin first. Also, a fixture at the WCS corner (a vise stop where the operator touched off) can give a false refusal ("cannot clear fixture") or a false fixture hit on a move that the machine never makes (`fixture_route.rs:105-116,137-142`). I found this from the code. I did not confirm it with a run.

Research result (part 2 of 2): the answers to the open questions.

**Where the defect shows.**
- Viewport, simulation, CL file and checks: yes, for each 2D and 3D milling path. The first move starts at (WCS X0 Y0, clearance) by design of #2382 (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:3109-3117`). The CL file writes it as the `START` line and as the `StartX/StartY/StartZ` params (`crates/post/src/post/mod.rs:275-279`).
- Posted G-code: no, in the usual case. The posts write move ends only, and the first traverse goes to the entry point at the clearance (`fanuc.cps:833-857`, goldens `nc/*/face_square_40x40.nc`, pin `crates/app/tests/wcs_start.rs:180-209`).
- Posted G-code: yes, when the fixture link router lifts the opening link. Then a `G00 X0. Y0. Z<H>` block is posted (`crates/app/src/operation/fixture_route.rs:186-229`). This is from the code. A run must confirm it (#2901 adds that pin).

**Calculation, post, or both.** The calculation. The posts are correct for the stream that they get. No post change is necessary.

**Does it depend on the operation type, the entry type, the machine file or the post dialect?**
- Operation type: yes. The 2D and 3D milling kinds that seed with `PathBuilder::approached(0, 0, clearance)` have it. Hole cycles start over the first hole (`crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs:63`). Turning, wire EDM, plasma and sinker paths seed at their own start. `seat_approach` leaves those paths alone (`crates/cl/src/cl/path_approach.rs:41-43`).
- Entry type: no. The seat moves only the start of the opening rapid. The lead-in, ramp and helix come after it.
- Machine file: only through fixtures (the router case above). The safe-retract settings (`G28` / `G53`) are machine-home moves, not WCS moves.
- Post dialect: no. All milling posts use the same first-traverse law.

**Same fault as #2382?** The same root, a different symptom. The generators seed at the frame zero. #2382 moved the drawn start from the world origin to the WCS origin. That keeps a start point that the machine never visits. The correct start is the entry column of the operation.

**Which test or fixture proves it.** `crates/app/tests/wcs_start.rs` already has the fixture: a plate away from the world origin, G54 on the stock corner, a face, a 3D finish and a drill. Its `opens_at` assertion locks the wrong law now. #2901 changes it to the new law, adds the WCS at the stock centre, and adds a fixture between the WCS origin and the entry.

**What stays unknown without a run.**
- The exact posted text for the fixture-router case.
- If a fixture at the WCS corner gives a false refusal in a real document.
- If the UI draws anything more than the first move of the path (I read only that the overlay draws the moves).

**Sub-issues.**
- #2901: Opening rapid of a milling path starts at the WCS origin: seat it over the entry point (`P1`, `effort:high`, `area:2d`, `area:3d`, `area:sim`).
- #2902: Simulation: the connector between two operations is one straight rapid; the posted program lifts Z first (`P7`, `effort:medium`, `area:sim`). Work it after #2901.

Research is complete. The sub-issues hold the work:
- #2901 (`P1`, `effort:high`): seat the opening rapid of a milling path over its entry point, not over the WCS origin.
- #2902 (`P7`, `effort:medium`): the simulation connector between two operations follows the posted order.

I removed `needs-research` and close this umbrella, so that Pick does not take it for code.
